answer: Coordination beacon pricing. Each agent must periodically solve a shared random challenge whose difficulty rises with the number of agents in the same behavioral cluster. The challenge is broadcast as a lantern signal, and answers are tagged with a per-agent cipher so clusters cannot share solutions without detection. A trellis of verified coordination edges is built from independent solutions; agents in dense clusters pay proportionally more compute. Attacker cost: N clones multiply challenge difficulty by N², making each sybil identity progressively more expensive to coordinate.
